'''''Batman Begins''''' is a 2005 [[superhero film]] based on the [[DC Comics]] character [[Batman]]. Directed by [[Christopher Nolan]], who co-wrote the screenplay with [[David S. Goyer]], the film stars [[Christian Bale]] as [[Bruce Wayne (Dark Knight trilogy)|Bruce Wayne / Batman]], with [[Michael Caine]], [[Liam Neeson]], [[Katie Holmes]], [[Gary Oldman]], [[Cillian Murphy]], [[Tom Wilkinson]], [[Rutger Hauer]], [[Ken Watanabe]], and [[Morgan Freeman]] in supporting roles. The film [[reboot (fiction)|reboots]] the [[Batman in film|''Batman'' film series]], telling the [[origin story]] of Bruce Wayne (Bale) from the death of his parents to his journey to become Batman and his fight to stop [[Ra's al Ghul]] (Neeson) and the [[Scarecrow (DC Comics)|Scarecrow]] (Murphy) from plunging [[Gotham City]] into chaos.

After [[Batman & Robin (film)|''Batman & Robin'']] (1997) was panned by critics and underperformed at the box office, [[Warner Bros. Pictures]] cancelled future ''Batman'' films, including [[Joel Schumacher]]'s planned [[Batman in film#Batman Unchained|''Batman Unchained'']]. Between 1998 and 2003, several filmmakers collaborated with Warner Bros. in attempting to [[Reboot (fiction)|reboot]] the franchise. After the studio rejected a ''Batman'' origin story reboot [[Joss Whedon]] pitched in December 2002, Warner Bros. hired Nolan in January 2003 to direct a new film. Nolan and Goyer began development on the film in early 2003. Aiming for a darker, more realistic tone compared to the previous films, a primary goal for their vision was to engage the audience's emotional investment in both the Batman and Bruce Wayne identities of the lead character. The film, which was principally shot in the United Kingdom, Iceland and Chicago, relied heavily on traditional [[stunt]]s and [[miniature effect]]s, with [[computer-generated imagery]] being used in a minimal capacity compared to other action films. Comic book storylines such as ''[[The Man Who Falls]]'', ''[[Batman: Year One]]'', and ''[[Batman: The Long Halloween]]'' served as inspiration.

Expectations for ''Batman Begins'' ranged from moderate to low, which originated from the poor reception of ''Batman & Robin'' that was credited with stalling the ''Batman'' film series in 1997. After premiering in Tokyo on May 31, 2005, the film was released in the United States on June 15. The film received positive reviews and ended up grossing over $375.6 million worldwide against a $150 million budget, becoming [[2005 in film|the ninth highest-grossing film of 2005]], and was the second highest grossing ''Batman'' film at the time of its release, behind [[Tim Burton]]'s [[Batman (1989 film)|''Batman'']] (1989). Receiving a nomination for the [[Academy Award for Best Cinematography]], the film elevated Bale to leading man status while it made Nolan a high-profile director.

Since its release, ''Batman Begins'' has often been cited as one of the most influential films of the 2000s. The film helped popularize the term ''reboot'' in Hollywood, inspiring studios and filmmakers to revive franchises with realistic and serious tones. It was followed by the sequels ''[[The Dark Knight]]'' (2008) and ''[[The Dark Knight Rises]]'' (2012), which rounded out [[The Dark Knight trilogy|''The Dark Knight'' trilogy]].

==Plot==
<!-- Per WP:FilmPlot, plot summaries for feature films should be between 400 and 700 words. -->
In [[Gotham City]], young [[Bruce Wayne (The Dark Knight trilogy)|Bruce Wayne]] falls down a well and develops a fear of bats. One evening, Bruce visits the [[opera]] with his parents and is so unsettled by the performers masquerading as bats that he asks to leave. While returning home, a mugger named Joe Chill demands possessions from Bruce's parents and shoots them dead during a botched robbery. Bruce is [[orphaned]] and raised by the family butler, [[Alfred Pennyworth]].

Fourteen years later, Chill testifies against mafia crime boss [[Carmine Falcone]], and is paroled. Bruce intends to murder Chill to avenge his parents, but an assassin in Falcone's employ kills him first. After confronting Falcone, who says real power comes from being feared, Bruce spends the next seven years traveling the world, training in combat, and immersing himself in the criminal underworld. In a [[Bhutan]] prison, Bruce is approached by [[Henri Ducard]], who recruits him into the [[League of Assassins|League of Shadows]], led by [[Ra's al Ghul]]. After completing his training, he rejects the League's mandate that all criminals should be killed. He burns down the temple and escapes after learning that the League believes Gotham is corrupted beyond saving and intends to destroy the city. Ra's is killed by falling debris, while Bruce saves Ducard.

Intent on fighting crime and redeeming Gotham, Bruce returns to Gotham and to his family's company, [[Wayne Enterprises]], which is being taken public by businessman William Earle. Company archivist [[Lucius Fox]], a friend of Bruce's father, allows him access to prototype defense technologies, including a protective bodysuit and the [[Batmobile#The Dark Knight Trilogy|Tumbler]], an armored vehicle. Bruce poses publicly as a shallow [[Playboy (lifestyle)|playboy]] while setting up base in the [[Batcave|caves]] beneath [[Wayne Manor]] and taking up the vigilante identity of "[[Batman]]", inspired by his childhood fear, which he has now conquered.

Intercepting a drug shipment, Batman provides his childhood friend, [[Rachel Dawes]], an Assistant District Attorney, with evidence against Falcone and enlists Sergeant [[Commissioner Gordon|James Gordon]], one of Gotham's few honest police officers, to arrest him. In prison, Falcone meets [[Scarecrow (DC Comics)|Dr. Jonathan Crane]], a corrupt psychologist who smuggles drugs into Gotham with his help. Donning a scarecrow mask, Crane sprays Falcone with a [[Scarecrow (DC Comics)#Fear gas|fear-inducing hallucinogen]], driving him insane and having him transferred to [[Arkham Asylum]] under his care. While investigating Crane, Batman is sprayed with the hallucinogen. He is saved by Alfred and Fox, who develop an antidote for it.

When Rachel confronts Crane, he reveals that he has introduced his drug into Gotham's water supply and drugs her. When Crane is captured, he claims to work for Ra's al Ghul. Batman saves Rachel and administers the antidote. At Bruce's birthday party, Ducard reveals himself to be the true Ra's al Ghul. Having stolen a powerful microwave emitter from Wayne Enterprises, he plans to vaporize Gotham's water supply, rendering Crane's drug airborne and causing mass hysteria that will destroy the city. He sets Wayne Manor aflame but Alfred rescues Bruce. The League of Shadows frees Crane and the other inmates from Arkham, while Ra's loads the emitter onto Gotham's [[monorail]] to release the drug at the city's central water source under [[Wayne Tower]]. Batman reveals his identity to Rachel before confronting Ra's on the train. Gordon uses the Tumbler's cannons to destroy the train track and Batman leaves Ra's to die as the train crashes.

Rachel now respects Bruce but refuses to be with him, promising they can be together when Gotham no longer needs Batman. Batman becomes a public hero. After purchasing a controlling stake in Wayne Enterprises, Bruce fires Earle and replaces him with Fox. Gordon is promoted to Lieutenant, shows Batman the [[Bat-Signal]], and tells him about a criminal who leaves behind [[Joker (playing card)|Joker playing cards]]. Batman glides away into the night to investigate. {{efn|Identified off-screen as the [[Joker (The Dark Knight)|Joker]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Moore |first1=Trent |title=Nolan explains how Batman Begins wasn't meant to set up a sequel |url=https://www.syfy.com/syfywire/nolan_explains_how_batman |website=[[SyFy]] |access-date=August 21, 2018 |date=January 14, 2013 |archive-date=August 21, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180821223120/https://www.syfy.com/syfywire/nolan_explains_how_batman |url-status=live }}</ref>}}

* [[Liam Neeson]] as [[Henri Ducard]] / [[Ra's al Ghul]]: <!-- DO NOT change this, per consensus --><br />The leader of the [[League of Assassins|League of Shadows]], an ancient society that uses chaos to punish the corrupt and decadent, who goes undercover as an associate of the League and trains Bruce in martial arts, later revealing himself in the film's climax. Writer David Goyer said he felt he was the most complex of all the Batman villains, comparing him to [[Osama bin Laden]]; "He's not crazy in the way that all the other Batman villains are. He's not bent on revenge; he's actually trying to heal the world. He's just doing it by very [[Draco (lawgiver)|draconian]] means."<ref>{{cite web|last=Ryan|first=Tom|title=In defence of big, expensive films|work=[[The Age]]|date=July 14, 2005|url=http://www.theage.com.au/news/film/defending-the-blockbuster/2005/07/14/1120934352863.html|access-date=August 26, 2007|archive-date=December 19, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081219051423/http://www.theage.com.au/news/film/defending-the-blockbuster/2005/07/14/1120934352863.html|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Gary Oldman]] was the first choice for the part, but ended up playing [[Commissioner Gordon|James Gordon]] instead.<ref name="vago">{{cite web |last=Vago |first=Mike |date=September 23, 2013 |title=Watch Christian Bale audition for the role of Batman |url=https://www.avclub.com/article/watch-christian-bale-audition-for-the-role-of-batm-103259 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141106190445/http://www.avclub.com/article/watch-christian-bale-audition-for-the-role-of-batm-103259 |archive-date=November 6, 2014 |access-date=November 6, 2014 |website=[[The A.V. Club]]}}</ref> [[Guy Pearce]], who collaborated with Christopher Nolan on ''[[Memento (film)|Memento]]'' (2000), reported that the pair had discussions about him playing the role, but both of them decided that he was too young for the part.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.empireonline.com/interviews/interview.asp?IID=1487 |title=Exclusive: Guy Pearce Webchat |work=[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]] |date=December 5, 2006 |access-date=September 3, 2012 |archive-date=May 15, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120515080047/http://www.empireonline.com/interviews/interview.asp?IID=1487 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Viggo Mortensen]] was also considered for the role.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Lyttelton |first1=Oliver |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2012/07/5-things-you-might-not-know-about-batman-begins-108292/|title=5 Things You Might Not Know About 'Batman Begins'|work=IndieWire |date=July 18, 2012|access-date=July 15, 2021|archive-date=July 24, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210724193948/https://www.indiewire.com/2012/07/5-things-you-might-not-know-about-batman-begins-108292/|url-status=live}}</ref> Neeson is commonly cast as a mentor, so the revelation that his character was the main villain was intended to shock viewers.<ref name=journeybegins>''The Journey Begins: Creative Concepts'' [DVD, 2005]</ref>
* [[Katie Holmes]] as [[Rachel Dawes]]: <br />Bruce's childhood friend and love interest who serves as Gotham City's assistant [[district attorney]] and fights against corruption in the city of Gotham. Nolan found a "tremendous warmth and great emotional appeal" in Holmes, and also felt "she has a maturity beyond her years that comes across in the film and is essential to the idea that Rachel is something of a moral conscience for Bruce".<ref name="pressconference">{{cite web|url=https://www.timeout.com/film/news/488/batman-begins-press-conference-part-two.html|title='Batman Begins' press conference, part two|access-date=August 23, 2012|work=Time Out – New York|date=June 16, 2005|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110909112618/http://www.timeout.com/film/news/488/batman-begins-press-conference-part-two.html|archive-date=September 9, 2011}}</ref>
** [[Emma Lockhart]] as Young Rachel Dawes.
* [[Gary Oldman]] as [[Commissioner Gordon|James "Jim" Gordon]]:<br />One of the few uncorrupted [[Gotham City Police Department|Gotham City police officers]], who is on duty the night of the murder of Bruce's parents and, in this way, shares a special bond with the adult Bruce and thus with Batman. Oldman was Nolan's first choice for Ra's al Ghul,<ref name="vago"/> but when [[Chris Cooper]] turned down the part of Gordon to spend time with his family,<ref>{{cite web|last=Adler|first=Shawn|title=Chris Cooper On His 'Batman Begins' Near Miss|publisher=[[MTV]]|date=March 4, 2008|url=http://moviesblog.mtv.com/2008/03/04/chris-cooper-on-his-batman-begins-near-miss/|access-date=March 4, 2008|archive-date=October 19, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151019111730/http://moviesblog.mtv.com/2008/03/04/chris-cooper-on-his-batman-begins-near-miss/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Nolan decided that it would be refreshing for Oldman, who is renowned for his portrayals of villains, to play the role instead.<ref>{{cite web|last=Thompson|first=Anne|title=Dark Knight Review: Nolan Talks Sequel Inflation|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=July 6, 2008|url=http://weblogs.variety.com/thompsononhollywood/2008/07/dark-knight-rev.html |access-date=July 7, 2008|author-link=Anne Thompson (film critic)|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080710052656/http://weblogs.variety.com/thompsononhollywood/2008/07/dark-knight-rev.html <!--Added by H3llBot-->|archive-date=July 10, 2008}}</ref> Speaking of his role as Gordon, Oldman explained, "I embody the themes of the movie which are the values of family, courage and compassion and a sense of right and wrong, good and bad and justice". He filmed most of his scenes in Britain.<ref>{{cite web|last=McClean|first=Craig|title=More Mr Nice Guy|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/3666071/More-Mr-Nice-Guy.html|work=The Daily Telegraph|date=June 23, 2007|access-date=April 23, 2010|archive-date=January 19, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100119005731/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/3666071/More-Mr-Nice-Guy.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Goyer said Oldman heavily resembled Gordon as drawn by [[David Mazzucchelli]] in ''[[Batman: Year One]]''.<ref name=journeybegins/>
* [[Cillian Murphy]] as [[Scarecrow (DC Comics)|Dr. Jonathan Crane / Scarecrow]]:<br /> A corrupt [[psychopharmacology|psychopharmacologist]] working as Chief Administrator of [[Arkham Asylum]]. A specialist in the psychology of fear, he has secretly created a [[Scarecrow (DC Comics)#Fear gas|fear-inducing toxin]] and plots with Ra's al Ghul to expose the entire Gotham population. Nolan decided against casting an Irish actor like Murphy for Batman, before casting him as Scarecrow.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Fleming|first1=Michael|last2=Dunkley|first2=Cathy|url=https://variety.com/2003/film/news/batman-bags-a-baddie-1117896986/|title='Batman' bags a baddie|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=December 10, 2003|access-date=November 2, 2006|archive-date=October 25, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131025023222/http://variety.com/2003/film/news/batman-bags-a-baddie-1117896986/|url-status=live}}</ref> Murphy read numerous comics featuring the Scarecrow and discussed making the character look less theatrical with Nolan. Murphy explained, "I wanted to avoid the [[Worzel Gummidge (TV series)|Worzel Gummidge]] look, because he's not a very physically imposing man – he's more interested in the manipulation of the mind and what that can do."<ref>{{cite news|last=Smith|first=Adam|title=The Scarecrow|url=https://archive.org/details/scarecrowspider00smit|url-access=registration|work=[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]]|date=July 2005|page=77}}</ref> [[Robert Downey Jr.]] was considered for the role.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/02/11/movies/robert-downey-jr-christopher-nolan-oppenheimer.html | title=Christopher Nolan, Robert Downey Jr. And Missed Connections | work=The New York Times | date=February 11, 2024 | last1=Ito | first1=Robert }}</ref>
* [[Tom Wilkinson]] as [[Carmine Falcone]]:<br />The most powerful [[American Mafia|Mafia]] boss in Gotham, who shares a prison cell with Joe Chill after he murdered Bruce's parents. Later, after having Chill murdered for his decision to testify against their relationship, he goes into business with Dr. Jonathan Crane and Ra's al Ghul by smuggling in Crane's fear toxins through his drug shipments over the course of several months so that they can be mixed in with the city's water supply.
* [[Rutger Hauer]] as William Earle:<br />The [[CEO]] of Wayne Enterprises, who takes the company public in Bruce's long-term absence.
* [[Ken Watanabe]] as decoy Ra's al Ghul:<br />A member of the League of Shadows assigned to impersonate Ra's al Ghul during Bruce's training.
* [[Morgan Freeman]] as [[Lucius Fox]]:<ref name=journeybegins/><br />A high-ranking Wayne Enterprises employee demoted to working in the company's Applied Science Division, where he conducts advanced studies in [[biochemistry]] and [[mechanical engineering]] and supplies Bruce with much of the gear necessary to carry out Batman's mission. He is promoted to CEO when Bruce takes control of the company by the end of the film.
Other cast members include [[Mark Boone Junior]] as [[Arnold Flass]], Gordon's corrupt partner; [[Linus Roache]] as [[Thomas Wayne]], Bruce's late father; Larry Holden as district attorney Carl Finch; [[Colin McFarlane]] as [[Gillian B. Loeb]], the police commissioner; [[Christine Adams (actress)|Christine Adams]] as Jessica, William Earle's secretary; [[Vincent Wong (British actor)|Vincent Wong]] as an old Asian prisoner; [[Sara Stewart]] as [[Martha Wayne]], Bruce's late mother; [[Richard Brake]] as [[Joe Chill]], the Waynes' killer; [[Gerard Murphy (actor)|Gerard Murphy]] as the corrupt High Court Judge Faden; [[Charles Edwards (English actor)|Charles Edwards]] as a Wayne Enterprises executive; [[Tim Booth]] as [[Victor Zsasz]]; [[Rade Šerbedžija]] as a homeless man, who is the last person to meet Bruce when he leaves Gotham City, and the first civilian to see Batman; [[Catherine Porter]] as an assassin posing as a reporter, who kills Chill under Falcone's orders; [[Risteárd Cooper]] and [[Andrew Pleavin]] as uniformed policemen; [[Jo Martin]] as a police prison official; and [[Shane Rimmer]] and [[Jeremy Theobald]] (the star and co-producer of Nolan's 1998 film ''[[Following]]'') as Gotham Water Board technicians. [[Jack Gleeson]], who had previously co-starred with Bale in 2002's ''[[Reign of Fire (film)|Reign of Fire]]'' and later found fame for his role as [[Joffrey Baratheon]] in the HBO series ''[[Game of Thrones]]'', appears as a young admirer of Batman who is later saved by him from Ra's al Ghul's men; Gleeson was cast at Bale's recommendation. Actors [[John Foo]], [[Joey Ansah]], [[Spencer Wilding]], [[Dave Legeno]], [[Khan Bonfils]], Mark Strange, Grant Guirey, Rodney Ryan, and Dean Alexandrou portray members of the League of Shadows. Hayden Nickel made his acting debut portraying [[James Gordon Jr.]]

==Production==
===Development===
{{further|Batman_in_film#Planned_relaunch|l1=Proposals for a fifth Batman film}}

In January 2003, ''[[Memento (film)|Memento]]'' director [[Christopher Nolan]] was hired by [[Warner Bros. Pictures]] to direct an untitled ''Batman'' film,<ref>{{cite web|last=Fleming|first=Michael|url=https://variety.com/2003/film/news/batman-captures-director-nolan-1117879566/|title='Batman' captures director Nolan|work=Variety|date=January 27, 2003|access-date=November 2, 2006|archive-date=May 2, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130502003542/http://variety.com/2003/film/news/batman-captures-director-nolan-1117879566/|url-status=live}}</ref> and [[David S. Goyer]] signed on to write the script two months later.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Brodesser|first1=Claude|last2=Dunkley|first2=Cathy|url=https://variety.com/2003/film/news/inside-move-wb-jumpstarts-batmobile-1117883691/|title=Inside Move: WB jump starts Batmobile|work=Variety|date=March 26, 2003|access-date=November 2, 2006|archive-date=October 6, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171006212112/http://variety.com/2003/film/news/inside-move-wb-jumpstarts-batmobile-1117883691/|url-status=live}}</ref> Nolan stated his intention to reinvent the film franchise of ''Batman'' by "doing the origins story of the character, which is a story that's never been told before". Nolan said that humanity and realism would be the basis of the origin film, and that "the world of Batman is that of grounded reality. [It] will be a recognizable, contemporary reality against which an extraordinary heroic figure arises." Goyer said that the goal of the film was to get the audience to care for both Batman and Bruce Wayne.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Graser|first1=Marc|last2=Dunkley|first2=Cathy|url=https://variety.com/2004/biz/news/the-bat-and-the-beautiful-1117899714/|title=The bat and the beautiful|work=Variety|date=February 8, 2004|access-date=November 2, 2006|archive-date=April 8, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170408001905/http://variety.com/2004/biz/news/the-bat-and-the-beautiful-1117899714/|url-status=live}}</ref> Nolan felt the previous films were exercises in style rather than drama, and described his inspiration as being [[Richard Donner]]'s 1978 film ''[[Superman (1978 film)|Superman]]'', in its focus on depicting the character's growth.<ref name=originalpsycho/> Also similar to ''Superman'', Nolan wanted an all-star supporting cast for ''Batman Begins'' to lend a more epic feel and credibility to the story.<ref name=journeybegins/>

Goyer wanted to [[reboot (fiction)|reboot]] the franchise; he and Nolan saw Batman as a romantic character, and Nolan envisioned a large, sweeping film like ''[[Lawrence of Arabia (film)|Lawrence of Arabia]]''. Although Warner Bros. required the film not be [[Motion Picture Association film rating system#MPAA film ratings|R-rated]], Nolan did not have a problem with this, as he wanted to make the film that he wanted to see when he was 11 years old.<ref name="greenberg20050508">{{Cite news |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2005-may-08-ca-batman8-story.html |title=Rescuing Batman |last=Greenberg |first=James |date=May 8, 2005 |work=Los Angeles Times |access-date=May 11, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081202014002/http://articles.latimes.com/2005/may/08/entertainment/ca-batman8 |archive-date=December 2, 2008 |url-status=live |page=E-10 }}</ref> His personal "jumping off point" of inspiration was "[[The Man Who Falls]]", a short story by [[Denny O'Neil]] and [[Dick Giordano]] about Bruce's travels throughout the world. The early scene in ''Batman Begins'' of young Bruce Wayne falling into a well was adapted from "The Man Who Falls".<ref name="genesis">{{cite video |people=[[Dan DiDio|DiDio, Dan]] (Vice President of DC Comics), [[David S. Goyer|Goyer, David S.]] (co-writer), [[Paul Levitz|Levitz, Paul]] (President – [[DC Comics]]), [[Christopher Nolan|Nolan, Christopher]] (director), Schreck, Bob (Batman Editor – DC Comics)|year=2006|url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0485650/|title=Genesis of the Bat |medium=DVD featurette}}</ref> ''[[Batman: The Long Halloween]]'', written by [[Jeph Loeb]] and drawn by [[Tim Sale (artist)|Tim Sale]], influenced Goyer in writing the screenplay, with the villain [[Carmine Falcone]] as one of many elements which were drawn from ''Halloween''{{'}}s "sober, serious approach".<ref name="genesis"/> The writers considered having [[Two-Face|Harvey Dent]] in the film, but replaced him with the new character [[Rachel Dawes]] when they realized they "couldn't do him justice".<ref>{{cite book|title=Absolute [[Batman: The Long Halloween]]|first1=Christopher|last1=Nolan|author-link1=Christopher Nolan|first2=David S.|last2=Goyer|author-link2=David S. Goyer|year=2007|isbn=978-1-4012-1282-7|page=[https://archive.org/details/absolutebatmanlo0000loeb/page/ §Introduction]|publisher=DC Comics }}</ref> Dent was later portrayed by [[Aaron Eckhart]] in the 2008 sequel ''[[The Dark Knight]]''. The sequel to ''Halloween'', ''[[Batman: Dark Victory]]'', also served as a minor influence.<ref>{{cite web|last=Vineyard|first=Jennifer|url=http://www.vh1.com/movies/news/articles/1494981/12172004/story.jhtml|title='Batman Begins' Scribe: 'We're Telling A Story That Has Never Been Told'|publisher=[[VH1]]|date=December 17, 2004|access-date=December 13, 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060830132547/http://www.vh1.com/movies/news/articles/1494981/12172004/story.jhtml|archive-date=August 30, 2006}}</ref> Goyer used the vacancy of Bruce Wayne's multi-year absence presented in ''[[Batman: Year One]]'' to help set up some of the film's events in the transpiring years.<ref>{{cite web|author=Stax|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/09/24/the-influences-of-batman-begins|title=The Influences of ''Batman Begins''|publisher=IGN|date=September 24, 2004|access-date=December 13, 2006|archive-date=August 14, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140814000948/http://www.ign.com/articles/2004/09/24/the-influences-of-batman-begins|url-status=live}}</ref> In addition, the film's Sergeant [[Commissioner Gordon|James "Jim" Gordon]] was based on his comic book incarnation as seen in ''Year One''. The writers of ''Batman Begins'' also used Frank Miller's ''Year One'' plot device, which was about a corrupt police force that led to Gordon and [[Gotham City]]'s need for Batman.<ref name="genesis" /> Due to [[List of Batman family enemies|Batman's extensive rogues gallery]] over seventy years, Goyer and Nolan decided to use the [[Scarecrow (DC Comics)|Scarecrow]] and [[Ra's al Ghul]] as the film's villains, as both characters had not been featured in previous ''Batman'' films nor in [[Adam West]]'s [[Batman (TV series)|1960s television series]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.digitalspy.com/movies/a109540/batman-scribe-rules-out-penguin-catwoman/|title='Batman' scribe rules out Penguin, Catwoman|last=Reynolds|first=Simon|date=July 10, 2008|access-date=September 1, 2021|work=[[Digital Spy]]|archive-date=September 1, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210901220232/https://www.digitalspy.com/movies/a109540/batman-scribe-rules-out-penguin-catwoman/|url-status=live}}</ref>

A common idea in the comics is that Bruce saw a [[Zorro]] film with his parents before they were murdered. Nolan explained that by ignoring that idea – which he stated is not found in Batman's first appearances – it emphasized the importance of bats to Bruce and that becoming a superhero is a wholly original idea on his part. It is for this reason Nolan believes other DC characters do not exist in the [[fictional universe|universe]] of his film; otherwise, Wayne's reasons for taking up costumed vigilantism would have been very different.<ref>{{cite web|last=Boucher|first=Geoff|title=Christopher Nolan says his Batman doesn't play well with others|work=Los Angeles Times|date=October 29, 2008|url=http://herocomplex.latimes.com/uncategorized/christopher-n-2/|access-date=October 30, 2008|archive-date=March 17, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130317003755/http://herocomplex.latimes.com/uncategorized/christopher-n-2/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Filming===
[[File:Batman Begins.jpg|thumb|Batman Begins scene where Batman burns]]
As with all his films, Nolan refused a [[second unit]]; he did this in order to keep his vision consistent.<ref name="batsuit" /> Filming began in March 2004 in the [[Vatnajökull]] glacier in [[Iceland]] (standing in for [[Bhutan]]).<ref name="batsuit" /> The crew built a village and the front doors to Ra's' temple,<ref name=discovery/> as well as a road to access the remote area.<ref name="batsuit" /> The weather was problematic, with {{convert|75|mph|-1}} winds,<ref name="batsuit" /> rain, and a lack of snow. A shot that cinematographer [[Wally Pfister]] had planned to take using a crane had to be completed with a handheld camera.<ref name=discovery/>

Unlike Burton and Schumacher's Gotham City that did not exist in the real world, Nolan shot exteriors in London, New York, and Chicago as he wanted the city to seem recognizable.{{r|greenberg20050508}} In seeking inspiration from ''[[Superman (1978 film)|Superman]]'' and other blockbuster films of the late 1970s and early 1980s, Nolan based most of the production in England, specifically [[Shepperton Studios]].<ref>{{cite news|title='Batman Begins' goes to the source|work=The Kansas City Star|date=June 25, 2004}}</ref> A [[Batcave]] set was built there and measured {{convert|250|ft}} long, {{convert|120|ft}} wide, and {{convert|40|ft}} high. [[Production designer]] [[Nathan Crowley]] installed twelve pumps to create a waterfall with {{convert|12000|impgal}}, and built rocks using molds of real caves.<ref name=locations>{{cite book|last=Kalindjian|first=Claudia|title=Batman Begins: The Official Movie Guide|publisher=Time Warner International|year=2005|pages=[https://archive.org/details/batmanbegins00dcco/page/144 144–45]|isbn=1-932273-44-1|url=https://archive.org/details/batmanbegins00dcco/page/144}}</ref> An [[airship hangar]] at [[Cardington, Bedfordshire]] was rented by Warner Bros. during April 2004<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/beds/bucks/herts/3506175.stm|title=Airship hangar is home to Batman|work=BBC News|date=February 20, 2004|access-date=November 2, 2006|archive-date=December 30, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081230014550/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/beds/bucks/herts/3506175.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> and, converted into a {{convert|900|ft|m}} sound stage, was where the slum-district of "the Narrows" and the feet of the monorails were filmed.<ref name=locations/>

[[File:Burned Helicopter (1).jpg|thumb|left|Burnt helicopter prop used in the film]]
[[Mentmore Towers]] was chosen from twenty different locations for [[Wayne Manor]], as Nolan and Crowley liked its white floors, which gave the impression of the manor as a memorial to Wayne's parents.<ref name=rise/> The building chosen to represent Arkham Asylum was the [[National Institute for Medical Research]] building in [[Mill Hill]], northwest London, England.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kasriel|first=Alex|url=http://www.times-series.co.uk/news/606532.0/?utag=8269|title=From leafy suburbs to silver screen|work=Edgware & Mill Hill Times|date=June 16, 2005|access-date=April 23, 2010|archive-date=August 7, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110807142950/http://www.times-series.co.uk/news/606532.0/?utag=8269|url-status=live}}</ref> The [[St Pancras railway station]] and the [[Abbey Mills Pumping Stations]] were used for Arkham's interiors.<ref name=locations/> The [[Senate House, London|Senate House]] of [[University College London]] was used for courtrooms.<ref name=locations/> Some scenes, including the Tumbler pursuit,<ref name="batsuit" /> were filmed in Chicago at locations such as [[Wacker Drive|Lower Wacker Drive]] and [[35 East Wacker]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.emporis.com/building/35eastwackerdrive-chicago-il-usa|access-date=April 23, 2010|title=35 East Wacker Drive|publisher=[[Emporis]]|archive-date=January 2, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140102100702/http://www.emporis.com/building/35eastwackerdrive-chicago-il-usa|url-status=usurped}}</ref> Authorities agreed to raise [[Franklin Street Bridge]] for a scene where access to the Narrows is closed.<ref name="batsuit" />

Despite the film's darkness, Nolan wanted to make the film appeal to a wide age range. "Not the youngest kids obviously, I think what we've done is probably a bit intense for them but I certainly didn't want to exclude the sort of ten to 12-year olds, because as a kid I would have loved to have seen a movie like this." Because of this, nothing gory or bloody was filmed.<ref name="pressconference" />

===Music===
{{main|Batman Begins (soundtrack){{!}}''Batman Begins'' (soundtrack)}}
The score for ''Batman Begins'' was composed by [[Hans Zimmer]] and [[James Newton Howard]]. Nolan originally invited Zimmer to compose the music, and Zimmer asked Nolan if he could invite Howard to compose as well, as they had always planned a collaboration.<ref name=knightmusic>{{cite news|last=Graydon|first=Danny|title=A Little Knight Music|work=Empire|date=July 2005|page=87}}</ref> The two composers collaborated on separate themes for the "split personality" of Bruce Wayne and his alter ego, Batman. Zimmer and Howard began composing in Los Angeles and moved to London where they stayed for twelve weeks to complete most of their writing.<ref>{{cite web|last=D.|first=Spence|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/06/10/batman-vs-hans-zimmer-james-newton-howard-part-1|title=Batman Vs. Hans Zimmer & James Newton Howard Part 1|publisher=IGN|date=June 10, 2005|access-date=December 1, 2006|archive-date=February 22, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130222033544/http://www.ign.com/articles/2005/06/10/batman-vs-hans-zimmer-james-newton-howard-part-1|url-status=live}}</ref> Zimmer and Howard sought inspiration for shaping the score by visiting the ''Batman Begins'' sets.<ref name="zimmer">{{cite web|last=D.|first=Spence|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/06/13/batman-vs-hans-zimmer-and-james-newton-howard-part-2|title=Batman Vs. Hans Zimmer and James Newton Howard Part 2|publisher=IGN|date=June 13, 2005|access-date=December 1, 2006|archive-date=October 27, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131027132509/http://www.ign.com/articles/2005/06/13/batman-vs-hans-zimmer-and-james-newton-howard-part-2|url-status=live}}</ref>

Zimmer wanted to avoid writing music that had been done in earlier ''Batman'' films, so the score became an amalgamation of orchestra and electronic music. The film's ninety-piece orchestra<ref name=knightmusic/> was developed from members of various London orchestras, and Zimmer chose to use more than the normal number of cellos. Zimmer enlisted a boy soprano to help reflect the music in some of the film's scenes where tragic memories of Bruce Wayne's parents are involved. "He's singing a fairly pretty tune and then he gets stuck, it's like froze, arrested development," said Zimmer. He also attempted to add a human dimension to Batman, whose behavior would typically be seen as "psychotic", through the music. Both composers collaborated to create 2 hours and 20 minutes worth of music for the film,<ref name="zimmer"/> with Zimmer composing the action sequences and Howard focusing on the dramatic scenes.<ref name=knightmusic/>

==Special effects and design==

===Design===
Nolan used the 1982 [[science fiction film]] ''[[Blade Runner]]'' as a source of inspiration for ''Batman Begins''. He screened ''Blade Runner'' to Pfister and two others to show the attitude and style that he wanted to draw from the film. Nolan described the film's world as "an interesting lesson on the technique of exploring and describing a credible universe that doesn't appear to have any boundaries", a lesson that he applied to the production of ''Batman Begins''.<ref>{{cite news|first=Pat|last=Jankiewicz|author-link=Pat Jankiewicz|title=Dark Knight Resurrected|work=[[Starlog]]|date=August 2005|issue = 337|pages = [https://archive.org/details/starlog_magazine-337JPG/page/n53 53]–57|url = https://archive.org/details/starlog_magazine-337JPG}}</ref>

Nolan worked with production designer Nathan Crowley to create the look of [[Gotham City]]. Crowley built a model of the city that filled Nolan's garage.<ref name=rise>''Gotham City Rises'' [DVD, 2005]</ref> Crowley and Nolan designed it as a large, modern metropolitan area that would reflect the various periods of architecture that the city had gone through. Elements were drawn from New York City, Chicago, and Tokyo; the latter for its elevated freeways and monorails. The Narrows was based on the [[slum]]mish nature of the (now demolished) [[Kowloon Walled City|walled city of Kowloon]] in Hong Kong.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Otto|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/06/06/interview-christopher-nolan-2|title=Interview: Christopher Nolan|publisher=IGN|date=June 5, 2006|access-date=November 6, 2006|archive-date=March 31, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120331134903/http://movies.ign.com/articles/622/622719p1.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Tumbler===
{{See also|Batmobile}}
[[File:BatmobileBegins.jpg|thumb|The Tumbler used in the film]]
Crowley started the process of designing the Tumbler for the film by [[kitbashing|model bashing]]. Crowley used the nose cone of a [[Lockheed P-38 Lightning|P-38 Lightning]] model to serve as the chassis for the Tumbler's [[turbine]] engine. Six models of the Tumbler were built to 1:12 scale in the course of four months. Following the scale model creation, a crew of over 30 people, including Crowley and engineers Chris Culvert and Annie Smith, carved a full-size replica of the Tumbler out of a large block of [[Styrofoam]] in two months.<ref name="batmobile">{{cite web|first=Marshall|last=Brain|url=http://entertainment.howstuffworks.com/arts/comic-books/batmobile.htm|title=How the Batmobile Works|date=June 16, 2005|publisher=[[HowStuffWorks]]|access-date=April 23, 2010|archive-date=June 25, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130625125343/http://entertainment.howstuffworks.com/arts/comic-books/batmobile.htm|url-status=live}}</ref>

The styrofoam model was used to create a steel "test frame", which had to stand up to several standards: have a speed of over {{convert|100|mph}}, go from 0 to {{convert|60|mph}} in 5 seconds, possess a [[steering]] system to make sharp turns at city corners, and withstand a self-propelled launch of up to {{convert|30|ft|m}}. On the first jump test, the Tumbler's front end collapsed and had to be completely rebuilt. The basic configuration of the newly designed Tumbler included a [[Chevrolet small-block engine|5.7-liter Chevy V8 engine]], a truck axle for the rear axle, front tires by [[Hoosier Racing Tire|Hoosier]] (which are actually dirt racing tires used on the right rear of open wheel sprint cars), 4 rear 44/18.5-16.5 Interco Super Swamper TSL tires (44" tall, 18.5" wide, mounted on a 16.5" wheel) and the [[suspension (vehicle)|suspension]] system of [[Trophy Truck|Baja racing trucks]]. The design and development process took nine months and cost several million dollars.<ref name="batmobile"/>

With the design process complete, four street-ready race cars were constructed, with each vehicle possessing 65 panels and costing $250,000 to build. Two of the four cars were specialized versions. One version was the flap version, which had hydraulics and flaps to detail the close-up shots where the vehicle propelled itself through the air. The other version was the jet version, in which an actual jet engine was mounted onto the vehicle, fueled by six [[propane]] tanks. The visibility inside the vehicle was poor, so monitors were connected to cameras on the vehicle body. The professional drivers for the Tumblers practiced driving the vehicles for six months before they drove on the streets of Chicago for the film's scenes.<ref name="batmobile"/>

The interior of the Tumbler was an immobile studio set and not actually the interior of a street-capable Tumbler. The cockpit was oversized to fit cameras for scenes filmed in the Tumbler interior. In addition, another version of the Tumbler was a [[radio-controlled car|miniature model]] that was 1:6 scale of the actual Tumbler. This miniature model had an electric motor and was used to show the Tumbler flying across ravines and between buildings. However, the actual Tumbler was used for the waterfall sequence.<ref name="batmobile"/>

===Batsuit===
[[File:Bale as Batman.jpg|upright|thumb|The Batsuit, as worn by Christian Bale|alt=A man in a batsuit, with a cowl on his head, a utility belt, and a cape flowing behind him.]]

The filmmakers intended to create a very mobile [[Batsuit]] that would allow the wearer to move easily to fight and crouch. Previous film incarnations of the Batsuit had been stiff and especially restrictive of full head movement. [[Costume design]]er [[Lindy Hemming]] and her crew worked on the Batsuit at an FX workshop codenamed "Cape Town", a secured compound located at Shepperton Studios in London. The Batsuit's basic design was a [[neoprene]] undersuit, which was shaped by attaching molded cream latex sections. Christian Bale was molded and sculpted prior to his physical training so the team could work on a full body cast. To avoid imperfections picked up by sculpting with clay, plastiline was used to smooth the surface. In addition, the team brewed different mixtures of foam to find the mixture that would be the most flexible, light, durable, and black. The latter presented a problem, since the process to make the foam black reduced the foam's durability.<ref name="batsuit" />

For the cape, director Christopher Nolan wanted to have a "flowing cloak... that blows and flows as in so many great graphic novels". Hemming's team created the cape out of their own version of parachute nylon that had electrostatic flocking, a process shared with the team by the [[Ministry of Defence (United Kingdom)|British Ministry of Defence]]. The process was used by the London police force to minimize night vision detection. The cape was topped by a [[cowl (mask)|cowl]], which was designed by Nolan, Hemming, and costume effects supervisor Graham Churchyard. The cowl was created to be thin enough to allow motion but thick enough to avoid wrinkling when Bale turned his head in the Batsuit. Churchyard explained the cowl had been designed to show "a man who has angst", so his character would be revealed through the mask.<ref name="batsuit" />

===Fight choreography===
[[File:Batman Begins action.jpg|thumb|On-set fight choreography act between Bruce Wayne and the League of Shadows]]
Fight choreographers for ''Batman Begins'', Justo Dieguez and Andy Norman, trained actors and stunt performers using the Spanish ''Keysi Fighting Method'',<ref>{{cite web|first=KFOrigin|last=Gould|url=http://www.fullcontactmartialarts.org/keysi-fighting-method.html|title=Keysi Fighting Method Origin|access-date=July 28, 2018|archive-date=September 13, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180913015725/http://www.fullcontactmartialarts.org/keysi-fighting-method.html|url-status=live}}</ref> which gained fame after it was used in the film and its sequel, ''[[The Dark Knight]]''; however, the method was modified in ''[[The Dark Knight Rises]]'' due to Batman's age and physical condition and in order to match Bale's fighting style. The method is a [[self-defense]] system whose training is based on the study and cultivation of natural instincts.<ref>{{cite web|first=KF|last=Gould|url=http://www.bloodyelbow.com/2012/7/19/3170123/dark-knight-rises-movie-christopher-nolan-batman-keysi-martial-art|title=Keysi: The Martial Art Of Christopher Nolan's 'The Dark Knight' Movies|work=Bloodyelbow.com|date=July 20, 2013|access-date=July 7, 2013|archive-date=August 30, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130830072407/http://www.bloodyelbow.com/2012/7/19/3170123/dark-knight-rises-movie-christopher-nolan-batman-keysi-martial-art|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Visual effects===
For ''Batman Begins'', Nolan preferred traditional stuntwork over [[computer-generated imagery]].<ref name=originalpsycho/> [[Scale model]]s were used to represent the Narrows and Ra's al Ghul's temple.<ref name=discovery>''Batman Begins: Path to Discovery'' [DVD, 2005]</ref><ref name=rise/> There were, however, several establishing shots that were CG composite images, such as Gotham's skyline, exterior shots of Wayne Tower, and some of the exterior monorail shots.<ref name=rise/> The climactic monorail sequence mixed live action footage, model work, and CGI.<ref name=save>''Saving Gotham City'' [DVD, 2005]</ref> The bats depicted in the film were entirely digital (except in shots containing only one or two bats), as it was decided that directing large numbers of real bats on-set would be problematic; dead bats were scanned to create digital models. Locations and sets were recreated digitally so that the flying bats would not appear incongruous once incorporated into the finished film.<ref name=save/>

==Release==

=== Context ===
{{See also|2005 in film}}

2005 was expected by industry experts to underperform compared to 2004. Many attributed the slump to be a result of high ticket prices, marketing costs, DVD sales hitting record levels, and new technologies creating an incipient demand for movies delivered directly via the Internet, over-the-airwaves, satellite dish or cable set-top box.<ref name="money.cnn.com">{{Cite web |title=Hollywood reels from box office slump - May. 11, 2005 |url=https://money.cnn.com/2005/05/10/news/fortune500/summer_movies/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050622075956/http://money.cnn.com/2005/05/10/news/fortune500/summer_movies/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 22, 2005 |access-date=August 27, 2022 |website=money.cnn.com}}</ref> By the start of the theatrical summer in 2005 (May), the box office slumped for 11 consecutive weeks, with year-to-date ticket sales down 5.4 percent from last year even as ticket prices rose a moderate 3 percent, to around $6.40 on average, according to Exhibitor Relations. Theater attendance prior to the summer of 2005 declined about 8 percent.<ref name="money.cnn.com"/>

Several films were projected to not only perform well at the box office, but also reverse the slump at the box office. ''[[Star Wars: Episode III – Revenge of the Sith]]'' was expected by the industry to be the top-grossing film of the summer due to being the final live action ''[[Star Wars]]'' film at the time. Other films that were expected to do well were ''Batman Begins'', ''[[Madagascar (2005 film)|Madagascar]]'', ''[[Mr. & Mrs. Smith (2005 film)|Mr. & Mrs. Smith]]'', ''[[Fantastic Four (2005 film)|Fantastic Four]]'', ''[[War of the Worlds (2005 film)|War of the Worlds]]'', and ''[[Charlie and the Chocolate Factory (film)|Charlie and the Chocolate Factory]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Summer 2005 Box Office Preview |url=http://www.boxofficeguru.com/summer2005preview.htm |access-date=August 27, 2022 |website=www.boxofficeguru.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Feelin' blue at the summer box office - Jun. 1, 2005 |url=https://money.cnn.com/2005/06/01/news/fortune500/boxoffice_slump/index.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050603014218/http://money.cnn.com/2005/06/01/news/fortune500/boxoffice_slump/index.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 3, 2005 |access-date=August 27, 2022 |website=money.cnn.com}}</ref>

''Batman Begins'' was expected by industry experts to help reverse the box office slump in June. However, there were concerns over a possible soft opening for the film. The previous film, ''[[Batman & Robin (film)|Batman & Robin]]'', was widely panned by critics and was credited with stalling the franchise since 1997. Bale's lack of star power at the time and a lack of iconic villains such as the [[Joker (character)|Joker]] and [[Penguin (character)|Penguin]] that were portrayed by A-list celebrities were seen as possible detachments from audiences.<ref>{{Cite web |title='Batman Begins' in the Shadows |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/article/ed3396797444/ |access-date=August 27, 2022 |website=Box Office Mojo}}</ref><ref name="Kelly-2005">{{Cite news |last=JOURNAL |first=Kate KellyStaff Reporter of THE WALL STREET |date=June 20, 2005 |title='Batman Begins' Fails to Break Movie Industry's Losing Streak |language=en-US |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB111923250139263805 |access-date=August 27, 2022 |issn=0099-9660}}</ref> Some also expressed concerns that Holmes' involvement with the film could derail the film's financial prospect due to her high-profile relationship with [[Tom Cruise]] (whose film ''War of the Worlds'' opened the following weekend) after his controversial appearance on ''[[The Oprah Winfrey Show]].<ref name="Kelly-2005" />''

=== Theatrical ===
Warner Bros. held the world premiere for ''Batman Begins'' in [[Tokyo|Tokyo, Japan]] on May 31, 2005.<ref>{{Cite news |date=June 7, 2005 |title=US premiere for new Batman movie |language=en-GB |work=[[BBC News]] |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/entertainment/4613279.stm |access-date=February 2, 2022}}</ref> The film opened on June 15, 2005, in the United States and Canada in 3,858&nbsp;theaters,<ref name="Mojo" /> including 55 [[IMAX]] theaters.

===Home media===
The [[DVD]] of ''Batman Begins'' was released on October 18, 2005, in both single-disc and two-disc deluxe editions<ref>{{cite web|first=John|last=Latchem|url=http://hive4media.com/news/html/breaking_article.cfm?article_id=7895|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051014014129/http://hive4media.com/news/html/breaking_article.cfm?article_id=7895|title=Batman Begins' Swoops Onto DVD Oct. 18|website=[[hive4media.com]]|archive-date=October 14, 2005|date=August 16, 2005|access-date=September 22, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> and also released on [[VHS]] and [[UMD Video]] formats.<ref>{{cite news|last=Chaney|first=Jen|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2005/10/17/AR2005101700863_pf.html|title='Batman': A Decent, If Not Heroic, DVD|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=October 18, 2005|access-date=July 13, 2008|archive-date=October 8, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181008113446/http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2005/10/17/AR2005101700863_pf.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In addition to the film, the deluxe edition contained featurettes and other bonus materials. The edition contained a small paperback booklet, the first ''Batman'' story, featured in ''[[Detective Comics]]'' #27, as well as ''[[Batman: The Man Who Falls]]'' and an excerpt from ''[[Batman: The Long Halloween]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www2.warnerbros.com/batmanbegins/synopsis.html|title=About the DVD|publisher=[[Warner Bros.]]|access-date=December 13, 2006|archive-date=September 22, 2005|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050922103008/http://www2.warnerbros.com/batmanbegins/synopsis.html|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Batman Begins'' achieved first place in national sales and rental charts in October 2005, becoming the top-selling DVD of the fourth quarter of 2005. The DVD grossed $11.36&nbsp;million in rental revenue.<ref>{{cite news|title=Top renters: week ended October 30, 2005.|work=Video Business|date=November 7, 2005}}</ref> The DVD held its position at the top of the sales chart for a second week, but fell to second place behind ''[[Bewitched (2005 film)|Bewitched]]'' on video rental charts.<ref>{{cite news|title='Begins' has 2nd a win under its utility belt|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=November 3, 2005}}</ref> The film had brought in $167&nbsp;million in DVD sales by August 2006.<ref>{{cite web|first=Pamela|last=McClintock|url=https://variety.com/2006/film/news/wb-mulls-superman-redux-1200342128/|title=WB mulls 'Superman' redux|work=Variety|date=August 13, 2006|access-date=July 7, 2013|archive-date=June 4, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130604053037/http://variety.com/2006/film/news/wb-mulls-superman-redux-1200342128/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Reception==
===Box office===
''Batman Begins'' ranked at the top in its opening weekend, accumulating $48&nbsp;million, which was seen as "strong but unimpressive by today's instantaneous blockbuster standards".<ref name="bom-shadows" /> The film's five-day gross was $72.9&nbsp;million, beating ''[[Batman Forever]]'' (1995) as the franchise high. ''Batman Begins'' also broke the five-day opening record in the 55 IMAX theaters, grossing $3.16&nbsp;million. Polled moviegoers rated the film with an A, and according to the studio's surveys, ''Batman Begins'' was considered the best of all the ''Batman'' films. The audience's demographic was 57 percent male and 54 percent people over the age of 25.<ref name="bom-shadows" />

The film held its top spot for another weekend, accumulating $28&nbsp;million in a 43 percent drop from its first weekend.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gray|first=Brandon|url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=1841&p=.htm|title='Batman' Sweeps 'Bewitched,' Swats Bug|work=Box Office Mojo|publisher=Amazon.com|date=June 27, 2005|access-date=January 25, 2008|archive-date=October 3, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071003190521/http://boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=1841&p=.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Batman Begins'' went on to gross $205&nbsp;million in North America and had a worldwide total of $371.8&nbsp;million from its original release.<ref name="Mojo" /> It earned $1.6&nbsp;million more from its 2012 re-release, bringing its lifetime worldwide total to $375.6&nbsp;million. It is the fourth-highest-grossing ''Batman'' film, {{as of|2012|August|lc=y}}, behind Tim Burton's ''[[Batman (1989 film)|Batman]]'', which grossed $411&nbsp;million worldwide and also being surpassed by its sequels ''[[The Dark Knight]]'' and ''[[The Dark Knight Rises]]'', both of which have grossed over $1&nbsp;billion.<ref name = franchises>{{cite web|url=https://boxofficemojo.com/franchises/chart/?id=batman.htm|title=Batman movies at the Box Office|work=Box Office Mojo|publisher=IMDB|access-date=February 21, 2020|archive-date=July 28, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190728112851/https://www.boxofficemojo.com/franchises/chart/?id=batman.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Batman Begins'' averaged $12,634 per theater in its opening weekend.<ref name="Mojo" /> It was released in more theaters, but sold fewer tickets than the other previous ''Batman'' movies, with the exception of ''Batman & Robin''.<ref name = franchises/> ''Batman Begins'' was the seventh-highest-grossing film of 2005 in the United States.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?yr=2005&p=.htm|title=2005 Yearly Box Office Results|publisher=[[Box Office Mojo]]|access-date=July 7, 2013|archive-date=January 17, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070117001752/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?yr=2005&p=.htm|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Critical response===
Review aggregator [[Rotten Tomatoes]] gives ''Batman Begins'' an approval rating of {{Rotten Tomatoes data|score}} based on {{Rotten Tomatoes data|count}} reviews, with an average rating of 7.7/10. The site's critical consensus reads, "Brooding and dark, but also exciting and smart, ''Batman Begins'' is a film that understands the essence of one of the definitive superheroes."<ref>{{cite Rotten Tomatoes|id=batman_begins|title=Batman Begins|type=m|access-date=November 11, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115152611/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/batman_begins/|archive-date=January 15, 2018|url-status=live}}{{RT data|edit}}</ref> At [[Metacritic]], which assigns a [[weighted mean]] rating reviews, the film received an average score of 70 out of 100, based on 41 critics, which indicates "generally favorable" reviews.<ref>{{cite Metacritic |id=batman-begins |title=Batman Begins |type=m |access-date=February 13, 2012 |archive-date=September 13, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140913172501/http://www.metacritic.com/movie/batman-begins |url-status=live }}</ref> Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "A" on an A+ to F scale.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cinemascore.com/ |title=CinemaScore |publisher=[[CinemaScore]] |access-date=April 14, 2022 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220413083139/https://www.cinemascore.com/ |archive-date=April 13, 2022 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="bom-shadows">{{cite web |last=Gray |first=Brandon |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=1837 |title='Batman Begins' in the Shadows |work=Box Office Mojo |publisher=Amazon.com |date=June 20, 2005 |access-date=July 7, 2013 |archive-date=December 20, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131220060347/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=1837 |quote=Moviegoers polled by CinemaScore gave Batman Begins an "A," while Fellman said it was rated the best of all the Batman movies in Warner Bros.' exit polling. }}</ref>
[[File:Christian Bale-7837.jpg|left|thumb|289x289px|Bale received critical acclaim for his performance in the film.]]
[[James Berardinelli]] applauded Nolan and Goyer's work in creating more understanding into "who [Batman] is and what motivates him", something Berardinelli felt Tim Burton's film had lacked; at the same time, Berardinelli felt the romantic aspect between Bale and Holmes did not work because the actors lacked the chemistry [[Christopher Reeve]] and [[Margot Kidder]] (''[[Superman (1978 film)|Superman]]''), or [[Tobey Maguire]] and [[Kirsten Dunst]] (''[[Spider-Man (2002 film)|Spider-Man]]'') shared in their respective roles.<ref>{{cite web|last=Berardinelli|first=James|url=http://preview.reelviews.net/movies/b/batman_begins.html|title=''Batman Begins''|publisher=ReelViews|access-date=August 28, 2007|author-link=James Berardinelli|archive-date=November 6, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181106201647/http://preview.reelviews.net/movies/b/batman_begins.html|url-status=live}}</ref> According to ''[[Total Film]]'', Nolan manages to create such strong characters and story that the third-act action sequences cannot compare to "the frisson of two people talking", and Katie Holmes and Christian Bale's romantic subplot has a spark "refreshingly free of [[Peter Parker]]/[[Mary Jane Watson|Mary Jane]]-style whining".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.totalfilm.com/reviews/cinema/batman-begins|title=Batman Begins – Film Review|work=[[Total Film]]|access-date=April 23, 2010|archive-date=May 2, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100502022850/http://www.totalfilm.com/reviews/cinema/batman-begins|url-status=live}}</ref>

''[[Los Angeles Times]]''{{'}} [[Kenneth Turan]], who felt the film began slowly, stated that the "story, psychology and reality, not special effects", assisted the darkness behind Batman's arsenal; he noted that Neeson and Holmes, unlike Bale's ability to "feel his role in his bones", do not appear to fit their respective characters in "being both comic-book archetypes and real people".<ref>{{cite web|last=Turan |first=Kenneth |url=http://www.calendarlive.com/movies/turan/cl-et-batman14jun14,0,4819786.story |title=Los Angeles Times reviews ''Batman Begins'' |work=Los Angeles Times |date=June 14, 2005 |access-date=September 4, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929134456/http://www.calendarlive.com/movies/turan/cl-et-batman14jun14%2C0%2C4819786.story |archive-date=September 29, 2007 |url-status=dead |author-link=Kenneth Turan}}</ref> ''[[The New Yorker]]''{{'}}s [[David Denby (film critic)|David Denby]] did not share Berardinelli and Turan's opinion. He was unimpressed with the film, when comparing it to the two [[Tim Burton]] films, and that Christian Bale's presence was hindered by the "dull earnestness of the screenplay", the final climax was "cheesy and unexciting", and that Nolan had resorted to imitating the "fakery" used by other filmmakers when filming action sequences.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Denby|first=David|url=https://www.newyorker.com/archive/2005/06/13/050613crci_cinema|title=Aiming Low|magazine=The New Yorker|date=June 5, 2005|access-date=August 27, 2007|author-link=David Denby (film critic)|archive-date=September 21, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070921012501/http://www.newyorker.com/archive/2005/06/13/050613crci_cinema|url-status=live}}</ref>
[[File:Katie Holmes 2011 (6024619824).jpg|thumb|Holmes' performance was criticized by critics, noting her lack of range and depth compared to the rest of the cast.]]
Michael Wilmington of the ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'' believed Nolan and Goyer managed to "comfortably mix the tormented drama and revenge motifs with light hearted gags and comic book allusions," and that Nolan takes the series out of the "slam-bang Hollywood jokefests" the franchise had drifted into.<ref>{{cite web|last=Wilmington|first=Michael|url=http://chicago.metromix.com/movies/review/movie-review-batman-begins/159537/content|title=Movie review: 'Batman Begins'|work=Chicago Tribune|access-date=September 13, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081204074616/http://chicago.metromix.com/movies/review/movie-review-batman-begins/159537/content|archive-date=December 4, 2008}}</ref> Comic book scribe and editor [[Dennis O'Neil]] stated that he "felt the filmmakers really understood the character they were translating", citing this film as the best of the live-action ''Batman'' films.<ref>{{cite web|last=Bray|first=Greg|url=http://www.batman-on-film.com/interview_dennyoneil_gbray_2006.html|title=Interview: DENNY O'NEIL|publisher=Batman On Film|date=October 18, 2006|access-date=August 27, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304054503/http://www.batman-on-film.com/interview_dennyoneil_gbray_2006.html|archive-date=March 4, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> In contrast, J. R. Jones, from the ''[[Chicago Reader]]'', criticized the script, and Nolan and David Goyer for not living up to the "hype about exploring Batman's damaged [[psyche (psychology)|psyche]]".<ref>{{cite web|last=Jones|first=J. R.|url=http://www.chicagoreader.com/chicago/whos-afraid-of-the-big-bad-city/Content?oid=919112|title=Who's Afraid of the Big Bad City?|work=[[Chicago Reader]]|date=June 16, 2005|access-date=April 23, 2010|archive-date=March 27, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100327161120/http://www.chicagoreader.com/chicago/whos-afraid-of-the-big-bad-city/Content?oid=919112|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Roger Ebert]], who gave mixed reviews to the previous films, and claimed in his review for ''Batman Returns'' that he did not believe noir worked in superhero films, wrote this was "the ''Batman'' movie I've been waiting for; more correctly, this is the movie I did not realize I was waiting for". Giving it four out of four stars, he commended the realistic portrayals of the Batman arsenal – the Batsuit, Batcave, Tumbler, and the Batsignal – as well as the focus on "the story and character" with less stress on "high-tech action".<ref>{{cite web|last=Ebert|first=Roger|url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/batman-begins-2005|title=Batman Begins|work=Chicago Sun-Times|date=June 13, 2005|access-date=August 27, 2007|author-link=Roger Ebert|archive-date=December 8, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191208214254/https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/batman-begins-2005|url-status=live}}</ref>

Like Berardinelli, ''[[USA Today]]''{{'}}s Mike Clark thought Bale performed the role of Batman as well as he did [[Patrick Bateman]] in ''[[American Psycho (film)|American Psycho]]'', but that the relationship between Bruce Wayne and Rachel Dawes was "frustratingly underdeveloped".<ref>{{cite web|last=Clark|first=Mike|url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/life/movies/reviews/2005-06-13-batman-begins_x.htm|title=Batman role fits Bale, but 'Begins' wears thin|work=USA Today|date=June 13, 2005|access-date=August 28, 2007|archive-date=July 25, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150725045749/http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/life/movies/reviews/2005-06-13-batman-begins_x.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Kyle Smith (critic)|Kyle Smith]] thought Bale exhibited "both the menace and the wit he showed in his brilliant turn in ''American Psycho''", and that the film works so well because of the realism, stating, "Batman starts stripping away each layer of Gotham crime only to discover a sicker and more monstrous evil beneath, his rancid city simultaneously invokes early '90s New York, when criminals frolicked to the tune of [[Crime in New York City|five murders a day]]; ''[[Serpico]]'' New York, when cops were for sale; and today, when [[psychopath|psychos]] seek to kill us all at once rather than one by one."<ref>{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Kyle|url=http://kylesmithonline.com/?p=349|title=Kyle Smith review of ''Batman Begins''|publisher=KyleSmithOnline|date=March 10, 2007|access-date=September 9, 2007|author-link=Kyle Smith (critic)|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201172556/http://kylesmithonline.com/?p=349|archive-date=February 1, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> In contrast, ''[[Salon.com]]''{{'}}s Stephanie Zacharek felt Nolan did not deliver the emotional depth expected of "one of the most soulful and tortured superheroes of all"; she thought Bale, unlike [[Michael Keaton]] who she compared him to, failed to connect with the audience underneath the mask, but that Gary Oldman succeeded in "emotional complexity" where the rest of the movie failed.<ref>{{cite web|last=Zacharek|first=Stephanie|url=http://www.salon.com/2005/06/15/batman_begins/|title=Salon reviews ''Batman Begins''|work=Salon.com|date=June 15, 2005|access-date=September 9, 2007|archive-date=July 16, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120716024158/http://www.salon.com/2005/06/15/batman_begins/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Film director [[Tim Burton]]—who had directed [[Batman (1989 film)|the 1989 Batman film]] and [[Batman Returns|its first sequel]]—felt Nolan "captured the real spirit that these kind of movies are supposed to have nowadays. When I did ''[[Batman (1989 film)|Batman]]'' twenty years ago, in 1988 or something, it was a different time in comic book movies. You couldn't go into that dark side of comics yet. The last couple of years that has become acceptable and Nolan certainly got more to the root of what the ''Batman'' comics are about."<ref>{{cite web|last=Ramey|first=Bill|title=Tim Burton Talks Batman|publisher=Batman on Film|date=April 13, 2008|url=http://www.batman-on-film.com/burton-talks-batman-in-amsterdam_4-13-08.html|access-date=April 16, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923182636/http://www.batman-on-film.com/burton-talks-batman-in-amsterdam_4-13-08.html|archive-date=September 23, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Impact==
''Batman Begins'' has been cited as one of the most influential films of the 2000s.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rosenfeld|first=Laura|title=5 Ways 'Batman Begins' Changed Hollywood Forever|publisher=Tech Times|date=July 19, 2019|url=https://www.techtimes.com/articles/58219/20150615/how-batman-begins-changed-hollywood-forever.htm|access-date=July 20, 2019|archive-date=November 18, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161118130454/http://www.techtimes.com/articles/58219/20150615/how-batman-begins-changed-hollywood-forever.htm|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Rothman|first=Michael|title='Batman Begins': 5 Ways the Movie Changed Hollywood|work=ABC News|date=June 16, 2019|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Entertainment/batman-begins-ways-movie-changed-hollywood/story?id=31802311|access-date=December 9, 2019|archive-date=July 26, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200726151554/https://abcnews.go.com/Entertainment/batman-begins-ways-movie-changed-hollywood/story?id=31802311|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Hayes|first=Britt|title=A Brief History of Movies Compared to Chris Nolan's Batman|publisher=ScreenCrush|date=July 8, 2016|url=https://screencrush.com/every-time-people-compared-their-movie-to-nolans-batman/|access-date=January 22, 2020|archive-date=July 26, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200726143555/https://screencrush.com/every-time-people-compared-their-movie-to-nolans-batman/|url-status=live}}</ref> On the film's 10th anniversary, ''[[Forbes]]'' published an article describing its lasting influence: "Reboot became part of our modern vocabulary, and superhero origin stories became increasingly en{{nbsp}}vogue for the genre. The phrase "dark and gritty" likewise joined the cinematic lexicon, influencing our perception of different approaches to storytelling not only in the comic book film genre but in all sorts of other genres as well."<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/markhughes/2015/07/30/exclusive-christopher-nolan-talks-batman-begins-10th-anniversary/#797eaf2329a0 |title=Exclusive: Christopher Nolan Talks 'Batman Begins' 10th Anniversary |magazine=Forbes |access-date=February 28, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171003225206/https://www.forbes.com/sites/markhughes/2015/07/30/exclusive-christopher-nolan-talks-batman-begins-10th-anniversary/#797eaf2329a0|archive-date=October 3, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> Shawn Adler of [[MTV]] stated ''Batman Begins'' heralded a trend of darker genre films, that either retold back-stories or [[Reboot (fiction)|rebooted]] them altogether. Examples he cited were ''[[Casino Royale (2006 film)|Casino Royale]]'',<ref>{{Cite news |first=Jacob |last=Stolworthy |title=Batman Begins at 15: How Christopher Nolan's superhero film changed the fate of James Bond |work=The Independent |location=UK |date=June 17, 2020 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/news/batman-begins-james-bond-casino-royale-christopher-nolan-tenet-no-time-to-die-a9570041.html |access-date=June 17, 2020 |archive-date=June 17, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200617102026/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/news/batman-begins-james-bond-casino-royale-christopher-nolan-tenet-no-time-to-die-a9570041.html |url-status=live }}</ref> as well as the in-development ''[[RoboCop (2014 film)|RoboCop]]'', ''[[Red Sonja#Film adaptations|Red Sonja]]'', and ''[[He-Man|Grayskull]]''.<ref>{{cite web|last=Shawn|first=Adler|title='He-Man' Movie Will Go Realistic: 'We're Not Talking About Putting Nipples On The Trapjaw Suit'|publisher=MTV|date=August 14, 2008|url=http://moviesblog.mtv.com/2008/08/14/he-man-movie-will-go-realistic-were-not-talking-about-putting-nipples-on-the-trapjaw-suit/|access-date=September 3, 2008|archive-date=September 8, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150908150944/http://moviesblog.mtv.com/2008/08/14/he-man-movie-will-go-realistic-were-not-talking-about-putting-nipples-on-the-trapjaw-suit/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Themes==
Comic book writer and author [[Danny Fingeroth]] argues that a strong theme in the film is Bruce's search for a father figure, saying "[Alfred] is the good father that Bruce comes to depend on. Bruce's real father died before they could establish an adult relationship, and [[Liam Neeson]]'s Ducard is stern and demanding, didactic and challenging, but not a father figure with any sympathy. If Bruce is anyone's son, he is Alfred's. [Morgan] Freeman's Lucius is cool and imperturbable, another steady anchor in Bruce's life."<ref name=fingerothvfx>{{cite web|last=Fingeroth|first=Danny|title=Batman Begins: Redefining the Dark Knight|publisher=[[Animation World Network]]|date=June 15, 2005|url=http://www.awn.com/articles/reviews/ibatman-beginsi-redefining-dark-knight|access-date=April 23, 2010|archive-date=August 20, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100820103236/http://www.awn.com/articles/reviews/ibatman-beginsi-redefining-dark-knight|url-status=live}}</ref> Blogger Mark Fisher states that Bruce's search for justice requires him to learn from a proper father figure, with Thomas Wayne and Ra's al Ghul being the two counterpoints. Alfred provides a maternal figure of unconditional love, despite the overall lack of focus on a mother figure in Bruce's life.<ref>{{cite news|last=Fisher|first=Mark|title=Gothic Oedipus: subjectivity and Capitalism in Christopher Nolan's Batman Begins|publisher=Department of English at the University of Florida|year=2006|url=http://www.english.ufl.edu/imagetext/archives/v2_2/fisher/#13|access-date=October 13, 2007|archive-date=December 19, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081219050624/http://www.english.ufl.edu/imagetext/archives/v2_2/fisher/#13|url-status=live}}</ref>

Fingeroth also argues that a major theme in the film is fear, which supports the story of Bruce Wayne becoming a hero. Director Christopher Nolan stated that the idea behind the film was "a person who would confront his innermost fear and then attempt to become it". Fingeroth referred to this film's depiction as "the man with fear—but who rises above it". The theme of fear is further personified by the Scarecrow.<ref name=fingerothvfx/> The film depicts how fear can affect all creatures regardless of might. Allusions to fear are seen throughout, from Bruce's conquering of his demons, to becoming Batman, to the Scarecrow and his deadly fear toxin. The macabre, distorted images presented in the Scarecrow's toxin-induced hallucinations also express the idea of terror to an extreme.<ref name="rebuilds">{{cite web|access-date=July 13, 2008 |url=http://english.ohmynews.com/articleview/article_view.asp?at_code=261720 |title=Thrilling 'Batman Begins' Rebuilds Franchise |publisher=OhmyNews |date=June 14, 2005 |last=Orndorf |first=Brian |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151006014859/http://english.ohmynews.com/articleview/article_view.asp?at_code=261720 |archive-date=October 6, 2015  }}</ref>

<!-- comparisons -->
Critic Brian Orndorf considered ''Batman Begins'' "fierce" and "demonstrative in brood", giving the film an abundance of gravitas and energy. It strays away from the lighter fare of [[Joel Schumacher]]'s 1997 Batman film, ''[[Batman & Robin (film)|Batman & Robin]]'', which contained [[Camp (style)|camp]] one-liners throughout. The theme of fear is intensified with the help of the musical score by Zimmer and Howard, which also "eschews traditional heroic themes".<ref name="rebuilds" /> Also contrary to previous ''Batman'' films, a psychological investigation of Bruce Wayne's split personality in the bat suit is only lightly touched upon. Orndorf noted that Bruce is a "character constantly striving to do the right thing, not worn down by incessant reexamination".<ref name="rebuilds" />
